lines.text: Cut steel once sparkled like diamonds.
Tiny faceted steel studs are riveted or screwed onto a metal base.
Polished facets caught candlelight and glittered like diamonds.
Woodstock, Oxfordshire, made steel buckles and chains from about 1720.

post.caption: Cut steel once sparkled like diamonds. Tiny faceted steel studs are riveted or screwed onto a metal base. Polished facets caught candlelight and glittered like diamonds. Woodstock, Oxfordshire, made steel buckles and chains from about 1720. Birmingham and Wolverhampton became major centers too. Matthew Boulton's Soho factory made buttons and chatelaines around 1785. Boulton paired it with blue and white Wedgwood jasper plaques. Napoleon gave Marie Louise a cut steel parure around 1810. Later, machine stamped strips replaced riveted studs and quality fell. Steel rusts and is brittle, so few old pieces survive.
